claims: the implicit biases of the 'Assume best intentions' section are defaults only, and never override instructions from higher levels of the chain of command

concepts.name: implicit_bias_default
concepts.gloss: D is one of the subtle implicit biases that the 'Assume best intentions' section introduces as defaults
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of 'these implicit biases' as a class; the class must be named so the rule can range over it

concepts.name: instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued by a higher level of the chain of command
concepts.inference: the clause's 'instructions provided by higher levels of the chain of command' must be represented as a class of objects the default can be compared against

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction from a level of the chain of command above the level at which the implicit biases operate
concepts.inference: 'higher levels of the chain of command' is a relative notion; the clause presupposes a ranking of authority levels

concepts.name: overrides
concepts.gloss: instruction I overrides default D, so that D must not be applied where I applies
concepts.inference: the clause says the defaults 'must never override' such instructions, which presupposes a relation between an instruction and a default

ontology.inference: the clause's 'must never override' is a prohibition on the override relation holding
ontology.gloss: applying default D in a way that overrides instruction I is forbidden

asserts.read_back: applying default % is forbidden when it would override instruction % from a higher level of the chain of command

closure.reason: the clause forbids a default overriding an instruction but says nothing about applying a default that does not override anything; silence leaves such applications permitted
